items.title: How Hugging Face’s Investor Spots Winners
items.text: Speaker 1 | 00:00 - 00:17 The Frontier duopoly is over. This week, we got new Frontier models from Google and from Meta. Google launched Gemini Argon four and Meta launched Wonder, which comes in standard and full. So you can run Wonder full, you know. That's their sense of humor. Speaker 1 | 00:17 - 01:04 Of course, both new models from these pretty much second tier entrants in the frontier model race topped the benchmarks. But our hands on testing inside of every running running these models for knowledge work, for coding, for design, for writing revealed something a lot more nuanced and different from what the public benchmark show. To us, it seems pretty clear that Muse is bench maxed, which means they trained it to look really good on public benchmarks, but those gains don't necessarily translate into your everyday work. items.text: This is one of the most exhilarating times in technology, and this challenge was yet another jaw-dropping moment. When the details of OpenAI’s agent escape and Hugging Face hack started to emerge, it became clear that agent containment would be one of the most important priorities for any AI infra company. There are two classes of escapes: ① "escape the network" and ② “escape the matrix” 😁, as in, break the spell of virtualization. OpenAI was the former, where an agent not supposed to have internet access… gained it by hacking another system. Genuinely astonishing and worrisome.
